issue_context.title: lightning: use sql to add secondary indexes
issue_context.body:
## Enhancement

In TiDB v6.5.0, the [index acceleration](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/v6.6/system-variables#tidb_ddl_enable_fast_reorg-new-in-v630) feature becomes generally available (GA), which improves the performance of adding indexes by about 10 times compared with v6.1.0.

After doing some tests, we found that the performance of adding indexes using SQL and the performance of importing indexes using lightning local backend is similar.
In tests, we imported 562GiB source files into a table. The table has one clustered primary key and four secondary indexes. We used the following two methods to add indexes to the table:
1. Use lightning to import data and indexes into the table.
2. Use lightning to import data only, and then use SQL to add indexes to the table.

The result shows that the two methods have similar performance. The first method takes 22m11s to add a single index while the second method takes 27m16s. There is no significant difference between the two methods.

Therefore, we can consider using SQL to add secondary indexes, which makes the architecture of lightning more simple and clear. Especially in large imports, this method provides more visibility and allows us to better control the import process.
